_comment: ngsolve contact#1 (active set is more accurate than pure penalty; penalty has an O(1/gamma) gap floor). Run 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604: the same obstacle problem solved twice on one mesh (maxh 0.2, elastic block E=1000 nu=0.3 fixed on top, body force 150, floor 0.01 below). Penalty through ngsolve.solvers.Newton over gamma 1e4..1e9 converges every time (status 0, 3 iterations) yet never reaches zero gap; the log-log slope of gap against gamma is -0.987, an O(1/gamma) floor, and the tightest gamma still leaves 7.2e-8. A primal active-set iteration on the assembled system -- bottom-edge y-DOFs in the active set held at exactly -G0 as extra Dirichlet data, membership updated from the sign of the reaction and of the remaining gap -- settles on a repeated active set in 2 outer iterations with a violation of exactly 0.0. Two departures from the claim's wording recorded: the floor exponent is measured rather than assumed, and the outer-iteration count is 2, below the claim's stated 3-10 range, so the fixture asserts the ceiling only. Mutations, both run: holding the active DOFs at -1.5*G0 instead of -G0 leaves a nonzero violation and the fixture fails on active_set_violation_is_exactly_zero and active_set_beats_every_penalty_gamma; flattening the gamma sweep to a single value destroys the slope measurement and it fails on penalty_floor_is_order_one_over_gamma. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 sets ACTIVE_LEVEL to -1.5*G0 instead of -G0, so the active bottom DOFs are pinned below the obstacle rather than on it and the equality that makes the violation exact no longer holds (this is the first of the two mutations recorded above; the gamma-sweep flattening is not wired to the hook). Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604: the unmutated run matches all 8 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 removes 'active_set_violation_is_exactly_zero=True' and 'active_set_beats_every_penalty_gamma=True' (and prints the forbidden 'FAIL:') so the fixture goes red. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py CAVEAT found while adding the mutation control (assertions NOT changed): 'active_set_violation_is_exactly_zero' is 0.0 == 0.0 by construction. The run reports active_set_size=6 of 6 bottom dofs, i.e. EVERY bottom dof is Dirichlet-clamped at exactly -G0 and excluded from free, so the solve never touches those entries and each term of viol = max([0.0] + [-(gfu.vec[i] + G0) ...]) is exactly -(-G0+G0) = 0.0, on top of a floor at 0.0. 'active_set_beats_every_penalty_gamma' (0.0 < 7.16e-8) inherits it, and 'active_set_is_a_strict_subset_or_all' only tests non-emptiness since nxt is a subset of bottom by construction. The docstring's last bullet -- that the active set matches the contact set of the tightest penalty solve -- is never computed. The penalty half of the fixture (slope -0.987, positive gaps at every gamma) is measured and sound.
